title: METR finds Anthropic's progress doubled — mostly AI, mostly redacted
summary: METR's independent assessment finds Anthropic improving its models on well-specified tasks at about twice its earlier rate, mostly because of AI, while most of the evidence stays redacted; Ajeya Cotra and Arjun Panickssery pull it in opposite directions. Then Anthropic's agent-memory post: transcripts, notes, wikis, and the offline 'dreaming' pass that checks notes against what happened.

topics: METR independent assessment of AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic (5 Nov 2026, updated 6 Nov; Cunningham, Rush, Whitfill, Wijk; 2.5 FTE, 12 Aug-29 Oct): AECI growth since Oct 2025 1.9x the earlier rate (95% CI 1.5-2.8x; robustness 1.1-2.9x), 'around twice the rate', 1.3x-3x not surprising; confident not due to training-compute scaling; ~80% of current acceleration attributed to AI; self-reported uplift ~12x called very loose evidence; no model access; Anthropic redacted a majority of the most informative evidence, cancelled a compute-allocation component; top internal model above 50% on every AECI benchmark (saturation worry); Claude involved in many stages. Reactions: Ajeya Cotra (Planned Obsolescence) says the RSP 'dramatically accelerated progress' threshold has already been crossed and naive compounding implies extreme superintelligence within a year; Arjun Panickssery (LessWrong) says model research judgment is 'very poor in a basic way' outside fast-feedback hill-climbing. Amdahl's-law reading of the 12x vs 2x gap offered as the hosts' own

Anthropic 'The components of agent memory' (Lance Martin, 6 Nov 2026): four layers (transcripts, notes, representations such as wikis, injected context); dreaming as an offline pass that checks notes against transcripts, merges, builds wikis, promotes and demotes; Pokémon (corrected Poké Center note reached Cerulean at action 1,935; Sonnet 3.7's 413 files/one badge vs Fable 5's 10 files/four badges); CL-Bench database task (Opus 5.5 0.655->0.838; Sonnet 4.6 0.330->0.364, 0.641 with a read-memory instruction); Stainless wiki 13%->48% over 128 sessions, wiki+search 61% vs search 53%; contract terms shared table 41/57 vs one agent per contract verbatim 57/57; 'record only failures' cut gains; Claude Code loads the first 200 lines or 25 KB of MEMORY.md

dives.story: Anthropic's components of agent memory and dreaming
dives.why_it_matters: Practitioners building long-running agents get a measured design for what to write down and how to keep notes honest, a direct hit on the retrieval and production-agents priorities; carried by two Anthropic feeds.

concepts_taught: measuring AI R&D acceleration as a change in the slope of a stitched capability index (Anthropic's AECI), separating compute scaling from attribution, and Amdahl's law as why ~12x self-reported uplift can coexist with ~2x measured acceleration

agent memory as a four-layer hierarchy (transcripts, notes, wiki-style representations, injected context) where the upper layers are rewrites rather than copies, so an offline 'dreaming' pass must check notes against the transcript as source of truth

lore.note: Alan admitted his home harness has kept an agent-written notes file for months, and although his logging proxy holds the full transcripts, he has never once checked a note against them — 'receipts, again; filed, not read.'
